_comment: Every built-in component type, in the order the Add-component dialog offers them. A type is added by writing its file beside this one and listing it here; the shaded JAR has no directory listing to discover it from. In a type file, each metric's 'queries' holds one query per backend (text, never empty), and its optional 'names' holds, per tool (telegraf, datadog, otel, cloudwatch), {metric, kind: gauge|counter|rate|sum-per-period, scale, note} - or null where that tool has no single metric for it (a ratio, a difference or a sum of its metrics, or nothing at all: the tester exports the computed series under the catalogue's own name). A name is written as its tool's export writes it: telegraf '<measurement>.<field>' (what --csv-columns metric=_measurement+_field joins), datadog and otel the metric's own name, cloudwatch '<Namespace>:<MetricName>' (AWS/EC2:CPUCreditBalance, CWAgent:mem_used_percent) with the statistic and dimension in the note. A note is one line of at most 160 characters saying which of the tool's series to export when the name is not enough: a tag filter, a fold, an input that is off by default. A metric with no prometheus query is known by the neutral identity <type>:<metric>{match}, which only a CSV collection can answer. Catalogue.readMetric refuses a malformed entry; CatalogueTest holds each tool's naming convention and that a metric with no prometheus query names some tool's metric or, where every tool it declares is null, ends its description by saying how to compute it: 'No single <Tool> metric: <what to combine, and how>, and export the result as <name>.'
